requestedActions.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination
Authorize the individual customer account via OAuth on their own instance

guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 for third-party apps with user consent. Registration happens on the instance, and apps are created on /admin/applications, so the connected instance admin must register the app. Read the repo list via GET /api/v1/repos/search with page/limit pagination. No OAuth scope can restrict the token: third-party apps receive administrative rights and scopes are not implemented. Read-only use therefore depends on the app's own code and must be verified by request logs, not by token scope.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for List repository names visible to the connected person, with pagination. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth2 provider support is documented
findings.detail: Forgejo documents acting as an OAuth2 provider so third-party apps can access resources with the user's consent.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.

findings.title: App registration is instance-wide on the admin applications page
findings.detail: OAuth2 apps are created on /admin/applications for an instance-wide provider. Registration on each customer instance needs that instance's administrator.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance where the app is registered

evidence.quote: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth tokens carry administrative rights and no scope limits them
findings.detail: Third-party apps that obtain a user token have administrative rights, and OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented. Read-only use cannot be enforced by the token.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

findings.title: Scoped access tokens are separate from OAuth tokens
findings.detail: The docs state scoped or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2, so the read scopes in the token-scope docs do not apply to the OAuth grant.

evidence.quote: Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Repository search returns repos visible to the caller
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search defaults to including private repositories the user can access and all visibility levels, which fits listing visible repo names.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
Parameter is_private in query (boolean, optional): show only public, private or all repositories (defaults to all)

findings.title: Pagination uses page and limit with Link headers
findings.detail: Pages are requested with page and limit. The Link header gives next and last links when more than one page exists, and x-total-count gives the total.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

steps.title: List visible repository names with pagination (read only)
steps.detail: Call the repo search endpoint with the OAuth bearer token and continue with page=2 and so on until no Link rel=next header is returned. Expected: a JSON list of repos plus Link and x-total-count headers. Boundary check: only GET calls; confirm the request log has no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are read until no next Link is returned and the repo names match the test account's visible set.
